svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "The breathing system. Watch one breath in and one breath out."], [1, "Breathing in: the external intercostal muscles contract, moving the ribs up and out. The diaphragm contracts and flattens."], [3, "The volume of the chest increases, so the pressure inside falls below atmospheric pressure: air flows in."], [6, "Breathing out: the muscles relax, the ribs move down and in, and the diaphragm domes upwards."], [8, "The volume decreases, so the pressure rises above atmospheric pressure: air flows out."]]
svg.title: The breathing system and ventilation
svg.desc: Nasal cavity, trachea, bronchi, bronchioles, alveoli, lungs, ribs, intercostal muscles and diaphragm. Play: the ribs rise and the diaphragm flattens as air is drawn in, then the reverse.
svg.text: Front view, simplified. The lungs are shown cut open to show the airways.

g.data-info: Spongy, elastic organs surrounded by pleural membranes, which reduce friction as they move.
Smaller and smaller branches that end in alveoli.
Tiny air sacs where gas exchange happens: oxygen into the blood, carbon dioxide out.
Windpipe, held open by C-shaped rings of cartilage. Lined with ciliated cells and mucus that trap and remove dust and microbes.
The trachea divides into two bronchi, one to each lung.
Air is warmed, moistened and filtered by hairs and mucus.
The external intercostal muscles contract to lift the ribs up and out when breathing in.
Sheet of muscle below the lungs. It contracts and flattens when breathing in, and relaxes and domes up when breathing out.

g.text: • external intercostals contract: ribs up and out
• muscles relax: ribs down and in
Forced breathing out also uses the internal intercostals.
